classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the final distance is the southward component of the first journey, convert the bearing to an acute angle and apply cosine in the supplied triangle.

content.prompt:
Eleni drives 120 km on a bearing of $130^{\circ}$.
She then drives due west until she is directly south of her starting point.
How far is she from her starting point, correct to the nearest kilometre?

spec.description: Unlabelled right triangle with starting point upper left, turning point lower right and final point lower left. A dashed northward extension and clockwise exterior bearing arc retain the supplied 130° bearing.
spec.mathematics: The initial 120 km leg has direction 130° clockwise from north. The westward return ends directly south of the starting point. The acute angle between the southward vertical and initial journey is 50°.
spec.answerVisibility: The diagram shows only the supplied 130° bearing, 120 km distance and right-angle marker.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the distance south of the starting point.
$$\begin{align*}\theta &= 180^{\circ}-130^{\circ}=50^{\circ}\\\cos50^{\circ} &= \frac{x}{120}\\x &= 120\cos50^{\circ}\\x &\approx 77\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
Eleni is $77\text{ km}$ from her starting point, to the nearest kilometre.
